To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
• The most efficient shielding against neutrons is a combination of iron and borated polyethylene.
the best combination of shielding materials for a 40×40×160 cm 3 block is iron (20 cm) – BPE (20 cm, 1.2% B) – iron (20  cm).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimization of the ATLAS forward shielding in order to minimize the background in the ATLAS forward muon spectrometers.
the optimization of the ATLAS shielding in order to reduce the radiation dose to the detector and to the experimental personnel.
the optimization of the ATLAS forward neutron shielding and with the study of the effect of a segmented outer shield on the neutron and gamma fluxes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best shielding is the one with the largest possible thickness of BPE.
a pure PE shielding is the least efficient, while the LiPE one is the best.
the most effective shielding for the ATLS forward region is a combination of a thin layer of lead (2–3 mm) and a thick layer of BPE (10–15 cm) with a thickness of iron in the range 20–30 cm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a pure polyethylene shield is not effective enough against the fast neutrons and the gamma rays, while it is quite effective against the slow neutrons.
a pure iron shielding is not enough to protect ATLAS from fast and slow neutrons and γ -rays produced by the 4 GeV/c proton beam in the forward region.

the best neutron shielding for the forward region of ATLAS is the iron–borated polyethylene–iron–lithium filled polyethylene sandwich, which reduces neutron fluence by a factor of 10 3 and gamma ray flux by a factor of ∼100.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the most efficient shielding against neutrons consists of an iron inner layer and an outer layer of BPE, LiPE or LiPE/BPE.

the BPE and LiPE shields are very efficient in absorbing fast neutrons and that the combination of iron with BPE and Li, in particular with a segmented outer layer of BPE and Li shields, provides an effective protection against the slow neutrons and γ rays produced in the ATLAS forward calorimeter.
the use of BPE and/or LiPE in the outer layer of the ATLAS shielding can significantly reduce the dose rate in the ATLAS forward area.
